title: Architecture review
why: The codebase has grown through many parallel worktree efforts (native AirPlay 2/1 engine, per-app routing, groups, synced local playback, Sonos DACP, PTP daemon) without a holistic pass checking the pieces still cohere as one architecture.
what: Read AGENTS.md/SPEC.md and the actual source across AudiouterCore/ and AirPlayEngine/, map current architecture vs. documented architecture, flag drift, dead paths, or coupling issues; produce a written architecture review.
notes: 2026-07-26 Review complete + re-evaluated against post-merge main. Verdict: targeted refactor (4 boundary defects A-D), not rewrite. Doc: docs/notes/architecture-review-audio-routing-2026-07-26.md, merged main@fd820d5, re-eval@6e1c0d1 on claude/audio-routing-architecture-review-3f1eff (worktree memory-leak-investigation-396ac3).

title: UI & window-management consistency audit
why: The app ships five window/panel surfaces (popover, Settings, Groups, onboarding, Control Panel) built across different sessions; docs/plans/phase-3-findings/EXECUTION-REPORT.md notes visual polish was deferred for several of them, and windows sometimes conflict over which one shows on top or holds focus.
what: Audit the popover, Settings, Groups, onboarding, and Control Panel windows for both visual consistency (spacing, color, copy tone, control conventions) and window-management behavior (z-order, focus stealing, buried-window recovery); produce a prioritized punch list.

title: Competitor & feature-parity research
why: Alec wants to identify features comparable multi-room/AirPlay/casting apps already ship, or that their users request but the developers have not built, to ground later roadmap items in real gaps rather than guesses.
what: Survey competitor apps (Sonos, AirFoil, Rogue Amoeba SoundSource, Google Home, BubbleUPnP, etc.) and their public issue trackers/forums for commonly requested unimplemented features; produce a shortlist of parity candidates relevant to Audiouter (Bluetooth, casting, companion app, etc.)

title: Bluetooth output support
why: docs/plans/PLAN-UNIVERSAL-SYNC.md already designed BT as a first-class Device.Kind with 6 locked decisions, but zero BT code exists yet; Alec wants Bluetooth enabled as a supported output type.
what: Implement Bluetooth speaker output per PLAN-UNIVERSAL-SYNC.md: Device.Kind.bluetooth, IOBluetoothDevice connect/reconnect flow, per-device delayed AVAudioEngine sink synced to the PTP/AirPlay reference timeline, BT entitlement/TCC prompt; gated on the two hardware spikes (BT-SPIKE-CONNECT, BT-SPIKE-OFFSET).

title: iOS companion app
why: Alec wants a downloadable phone app that discovers the Mac over the local network (similar to how the Sonos app works) and controls output/groups/volume from a phone instead of requiring the Mac own UI.
what: Research and design a local-network control protocol plus iOS client (discovery, pairing, remote control surface for devices/groups/volume), starting with a design/scoping pass before implementation.

title: Cast-like output support
why: Alec wants parity with Google Cast-style casting so other apps/devices can cast audio to Audiouter-controlled speakers, not just AirPlay/Bluetooth.
what: Research feasibility of supporting a Cast-like protocol (Google Cast/Chromecast audio, or a custom equivalent) as an additional output or input path, and produce a scoping brief before any implementation begins.

title: Enforce routing scope exclusivity + cross-FIFO ordering in NativeBackend
why: T7 (roadmap 007, commit 86b02b7) fixed within-transition binding via AirPlayEngine.boundStreamId/rebindOutput but left two things unarbitrated: scope exclusivity between whole-system and per-app routing still relies only on the UI layer (GroupController), not enforced in NativeBackend; and ordering between the converging and bindTail FIFOs across an in-flight transition (not within one) is still unarbitrated.
what: Design and land the larger restructure T7 deliberately deferred: either a Swift-side arbiter for which domain wins when both want the same device, or a single serialization domain spanning both converging and bindTail for cross-FIFO ordering during in-flight transitions.

title: Add per-app tap device-identity dropout guard
why: T4 (roadmap 007, commit 4fe60fc) found PerAppCaptureCoordinator/CoreAudioProcessTap has no deviceMoved-equivalent compare, unlike NativeCaptureCoordinator whole-system tap; a per-app tap rebuilt onto a different device at the same rate could silently miss the RTP-session-reset window that TapReanchor closes for whole-system.
what: Give CoreAudioProcessTap a tappedDeviceID and wire it through TapReanchor (AudiouterCore/Sources/AudiouterCore/TapRebuildLifecycle.swift) so per-app redirects get the same silent-dropout protection whole-system already has.

title: Fix AudioDiag.log arithmetic-overflow crash on first call
why: AIRPLAY_AUDIO_DIAG=1 crashed the app on its first log line: DispatchTime.now().uptimeNanoseconds - startUptimeNanos underflowed because startUptimeNanos lazily initializes with its own later DispatchTime.now() call, evaluated after the LHS now. Pre-existing on main since 2026-07-24 (c51599a), only reachable with the diagnostic env var set.
what: Read startUptimeNanos into a local before reading now, and use wrapping subtraction (&-) as a second line of defense. AudiouterCore/Sources/AudiouterCore/AudioDiag.swift.

title: Exclude own render process while a .currentDevice per-app route is live
why: Redirecting an app to Play on this Mac while an AirPlay device is selected for the whole system muted it locally and sent it out the AirPlay device instead, because LocalPlaybackEngine renders .currentDevice routes into the same default output device the whole-system tap taps, and the tap never excluded our own render process (only the routed apps).
what: Added NativeCaptureCoordinator.setLocalPlaybackRenderPID(_:), mirroring the existing syncedLocalRenderPID self-exclude used for the play-everywhere sink. Wired from NativeBackend.updateAppRoutes off the existing localExcluded set.

title: Whole-system (stream 0) writes had zero backpressure telemetry
why: Alec reproduced audio stopping on the selected AirPlay device (meter still moving) with zero telemetry anywhere. NativeBackend.sampleWriteBacklogIfDue() only fires from routeMixer.onMixedBuffer (per-app, stream>=1); a session with no active .device route never samples engine.writeBacklogSnapshot() at all, hiding a genuine engine-side drop on stream 0.
what: EngineSink (NativeCaptureCoordinator.swift) now samples its own write_backlog_drop telemetry, path=wholeSystem, same 500-write delta-gated cadence. Diagnostic-only -- does not explain the drop itself, makes the next repro visible.

title: Fix reentrant dispatch_sync deadlock in DefaultOutputDeviceMonitor.start()
why: Connecting a Bluetooth device crashed the app: handleNotification() runs on the monitors own queue and calls a subscribers onChange synchronously, and a tap rebuilds onChange resubscribes via subscribeToDefaultOutput which unconditionally calls start(), a bare queue.sync onto the queue already executing -- libdispatch traps that as a deadlock (SIGTRAP).
what: Tagged the queue with DispatchSpecificKey and routed start/stop/current/deinit through a runOnQueue(_:) helper that runs inline when already on the queue. Introduced by todays T1/T2 (DefaultOutputDeviceMonitor), not pre-existing.

title: Rapid system-volume dragging desyncs Main Out mirror ratios
why: GroupController.mirrorSystemVolumeToMainOut holds a ratio snapshot only while held.commanded == currentMemberVolumes(members); Sonos volume write-back is a network DACP round-trip, not synchronous, so a fast slider drag can land a stale write-back read between mirror writes and force a re-derive on every tick instead of holding the snapshot -- visible as Main Audio and the Sonos row percentages drifting out of sync.
what: Investigate making the commanded==current comparison tolerant of in-flight DACP write-back latency (e.g. a short grace window, or ignoring a stale read while a write is outstanding) in GroupController.swift mirrorSystemVolumeToMainOut/currentMemberVolumes.

title: pollSchedulingSnapshot send_sched telemetry never fires (dead re-arm)
why: NativeBackend.pollSchedulingSnapshot() (NativeBackend.swift:3971-4002) only reaches its reschedule call (asyncAfter, :3999-4001) after its own guard self.started/self.captureRunning (:3972) passes, but it is armed exactly once from start() (:1240) before any device is ever selected. Confirmed: grep -c write_evt:send_sched telemetry.jsonl returns 0 across this machines entire history.
what: Re-arm startSchedulingSnapshotPolling() wherever captureRunning flips true, not just once at start(). AudiouterCore/Sources/AudiouterCore/NativeBackend.swift.

title: Investigate whole-system AirPlay dropout/judder under rapid volume changes
why: Reproduced live: dragging system volume rapidly while streaming to a selected AirPlay device causes judder then complete silence on that device, while the app own capture meter keeps moving. Telemetry (routing state, write-backlog) is completely clean through the failure window -- root cause unknown, not yet found.
what: Full investigation plan: docs/plans/PLAN-WHOLE-SYSTEM-AUDIO-DROPOUT-JUDDER-INVESTIGATION.md. Deliberately deferred, not tackled on the roadmap-007 branch per Alec.

title: Follow-main app silent after another app is redirected to This Mac
why: Reproduced live 2026-07-29 (telemetry sid C98DF1E0): with audio streaming to a Sonos Move, redirecting the only playing app to This Mac left the whole-system tap capturing and the engine writing, but the next unrouted app to press play was completely inaudible until the owner deselected and reselected the output device. Telemetry shows a measured 9.14 s gap with ZERO writes to stream 0 (send_sched gap_count frozen 15236 across 5.1 s, gap_max_ms 9136.8, write_cadence_drift deficitDeltaSeconds 9.146) starting at the exclusion-change tap teardown and ending when the second app started. The vendored sender advances RTP position by samples written (rtp_common.c:186) and builds the rtptime-to-wall-clock anchor from the producer pts on each write (airplay.c:2232,2257), so a producer stall injects a permanent skew the receiver never recovers from. resetAirPlaySessionForWholeSystem -- the only thing that re-anchors stream 0 -- has exactly two triggers (NativeBackend.swift:1389 device/rate rebuild, :2020 synced-local churn) and neither fires on write starvation. Deselect/reselect works only because it builds a brand-new session with a fresh randomized pos (rtp_common.c:75). Bug 6 in the 2026-07-26 onion chain.
what: Full investigation + fix plan: docs/plans/PLAN-REDIRECT-FOLLOW-MAIN-SILENCE.md. Investigation first, fix second. T-I1/T-I2 are owner live tests that discriminate the two surviving candidates (C1 producer-starvation gap with no re-anchor vs C2 the exclusion-change rebuild itself being unsafe to skip); T-I3 closes the observability gap (no telemetry fires when an unrouted app starts playing, and .capturing is set on tap-create success rather than first buffer); T-I4 reads the vendored sync path to decide whether a FLUSH re-anchor suffices. T-F1 (if C1) adds the missing third trigger for resetAirPlaySessionForWholeSystem, fired on the resume edge of a single long write gap, thresholded on one gap and never on cumulative deficit. NOT fixed on this branch by design -- research/plan/roadmap only, per Alec.
notes: 2026-07-29 Read-only research on claude/redirect-follow-main-silence (worktree .claude/worktrees/redirect-follow-main-silence, off main@2042de1). No code changed, no live test run by the agent. Corroborated across five days of telemetry: 25 of 25 exclusion-change tap rebuilds with an AirPlay device live were followed by no re-anchor within 6 s, zero counterexamples -- correct by design (AGENTS.md R10) for the 24 where audio kept flowing, fatal for the one that opened a starvation window. Candidates C4 (exclusion over-attribution), C5 (capture gate), C6 (one-role-per-speaker 7c2cf06 / launch-reset 7afb04c) are refuted by this telemetry, not merely deprioritized. OVERLAP WARNING for whoever schedules this: T-F1 touches the same write-cadence measurement 016 (judder investigation) owns -- the chronic ~3.3 ms/s deficit slide documented there would thrash a naive cumulative-deficit trigger, so the two must be reconciled before either lands. T-I3 also touches NativeCaptureCoordinator.swift alongside in-progress 012.

title: Connect-volume seed: prioritize device-reported / last-known volume over fixed default
why: Alec (2026-07-29): the connect seed today always uses a fixed connect-default (35%) on a user-initiated connect, a holdover from when the seed inherited the Macs system volume and could blast the user. He wants the priority reordered: (1) the device/system own reported current volume if available, (2) otherwise the level that device previously had in our system, persisted per device across restarts, (3) the fixed connect-default only as a last resort for a never-seen device. Only the user-connect branch changes; F-REBIND (out-of-band reconnect) already preserves the in-session level and is untouched.
what: Read-only research + plan: docs/plans/PLAN-CONNECT-VOLUME-SEED.md. Traces the current seed (NativeBackend.connectVolumeSeed, userConnectSeed, stashedVolume, known[id].volume), the wire/UI domain conversion setSpeakerVolume already demonstrates for a receiver-reported level, and the vendored AirPlay sender/receiver protocol. Feasibility verdict: no GET_PARAMETER or any pull primitive exists anywhere in the vendored C sender (0 matches); the sender is the protocols volume authority and only ever pushes SET_PARAMETER. The only receiver-volume signal is an asynchronous, receiver-initiated push (RTSP reverse /event channel or DACP setproperty, both already wired to NativeBackend), coded and documented as a change notification, not an initial-state announcement; whether any receiver fires one unprompted at connect time, early enough to beat the seeds own push, is unverified and needs a live hardware probe (T-I1). Persistence finding: known[id].volume and stashedVolume are in-memory only today, nothing is written to disk, so tier 2 (persisted last-known level) is new work, not a rename -- DeviceIconStore.swift is the direct pattern to copy (stable colon-hex device id, Codable versioned JSON, same Application Support directory). Also raises, without deciding, an anti-blast open question: a device reporting 100% reopens the exact blast risk the fixed default was built to close, so the plan proposes T-I2 as an owner decision between trusting tier 1 unclamped, a cheap ceiling clamp, or a genuine ramp. Task list separates investigation-remaining (T-I1 live protocol probe, T-I2 anti-blast decision) from implementation (T-F1 bounded-listen tier-1 mechanism, T-F2 DeviceVolumeStore, T-F3 write-through wiring, T-F4 rewire connectVolumeSeed, T-F5 tests, T-F6 docs), gated on the two owner decisions.
notes: 2026-07-29 Read-only research on claude/connect-volume-seed (worktree .claude/worktrees/connect-volume-seed, off main@2042de1). No code changed, no live test run by the agent. Two things need the owner before implementation starts: T-I1 (does any target receiver report its own volume unprompted, early enough in the connect sequence to use) and T-I2 (the anti-blast clamp-vs-ramp-vs-trust decision for a device-reported value). DeviceVolumeStore (T-F2) is independent of both and can be built in parallel.

title: BT-mic (HFP) trigger causes app<->Bluetooth rebuild oscillation with audible drops
why: Reproduced live 2026-07-29 ~19:40 (telemetry sid C98DF1E0): triggering the Bluetooth microphone (HFP mode) while streaming caused a rebuild ping-pong — 16000Hz rebuild+session_reset at 19:40:01, 44100Hz rebuild+session_reset at 19:40:23, another device_change + rebuild 2s later with rebind_recover_flush noop_fallback. Each of our tap rebuilds touches the BT device mid-renegotiation, likely re-perturbing it (our private tap-aggregate includes the BT device as a whole sub-device, input side unrestricted — NativeCaptureCoordinator.swift createAggregate ~:2263 — so aggregate IO may itself engage the mic path and force/prolong HFP). Owner: big drop + back-and-forth disconnect between app and Bluetooth; not urgent but must be addressed.
notes: Same BT/HFP family as the 16kHz corpse-pin found the same evening (rebuild during BT teardown pinned capture at 16000 for 16s) and shares fix surface with docs/plans/PLAN-CONSISTENT-MAINOUT-RATE-PIN.md (on main) and roadmap 016/017. Candidate directions: treat 16000Hz as a known HFP settling marker and defer rebuilds while the device renegotiates; widen/rate-aware settle window for HFP transitions; restrict the tap-aggregate sub-device to output streams so our own IO cannot engage the BT mic. Evidence preserved in telemetry sid C98DF1E0 19:40:01-19:40:27.
